definition: In computer vision, photo-consistency determines whether a given voxel is occupied.
details: A voxel is considered to be photo consistent when its color appears to be similar to all the cameras that can see it. Most voxel coloring or space carving techniques require using photo consistency as a check condition in Image-based modeling and rendering applications.

explainer.lead: Photo-consistency tests whether a point in 3D space looks the same from every camera that sees it, deciding if a voxel is occupied. It matters as the core check in image-based reconstruction.

tiers.eli5: If a tiny cube of space looks the same colour from every camera angle, the system assumes something is really there.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as the occupancy test in voxel colouring and space carving. Pitfall: shiny or textureless surfaces look inconsistent across views and get carved away.
tiers.paperLevel: A voxel is photo-consistent when its colour is similar across all cameras that observe it; most voxel colouring and space carving methods use this as a check condition. Limits: specular surfaces and occlusion break the assumption.

explainer.example: A voxel whose colour matches in five calibrated views is kept; one colour that differs in even a single view is carved out.
